summary: Mabel Haynes Bode (1864–1922) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She studied at Notting Hill and Ealing High School, University College London, under T. W. Rhys Davids (~1893–1905), and at the University of Bern (~1905–1908). She held posts at UCL (~1912–1917) and SOAS (~1917–1922).

Madeleine Biardeau (1922–2010) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at École Normale Supérieure de Sèvres/de jeunes filles (~1943–1946) and the University of Kerala (~1952–1954). She served as an instructor at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1958–1989).

Madhav M. Deshpande (born 1946) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a professor at the University of Michigan, with his position attested in 1976 and from 2006 to 2009.

Madhav Sadashiv Gore (1921–2010) studied at the University of Mumbai (~1940–1944), under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (~1946–1960), and at Columbia University School of Social Work (~1951–1961). He held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1980–1982).
Madhu Khanna is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. In 2012, she held attested posts at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Madhukar Anant Mehendale (1918–2020) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and as Professor of Sanskrit and Sanskrit (Vedic) Literature at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1970, 1983, 2026).

Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky (1927–2016) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After graduating from Fergusson College (~1947–1951), he founded the Archeology Research Group in 1951 and served as Associate Director (1976–1996) and director emeritus of research (~1976–2005) at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Maha Chakri Sirindhorn (born 1955) works in Indology, history and archaeology, and Sinology. Educated at Chitralada School, Chulalongkorn, Silpakorn (under Satya Vrat Shastri), Srinakharinwirot, the Asian Institute of Technology, and Peking University, she holds an M.A. in Oriental Epigraphy (1977–1979).

Mahasi Sayadaw (1904–1982) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Aletawya Sayadaw, Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw U Narada, and Thelon Sayadaw. He was abbot of Mawlamyine Monastery (1941), resident teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha (1947), and founded the Insight Meditation Society (1979).

Mahendranath Gupta (1854–1932) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at Hare School, the University of Calcutta, and Presidency University (~1871–1875), he held posts as a professor at Ripon College and Surendranath College from ~1885 to 1932.

Mahesh A. Deokar works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He has served as Professor (attested 2011) and Head (attested 2020–2021) at Savitribai Phule Pune University, and as Regional Representative for the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).

Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya (1836–1906) was an Indology scholar who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested in 1882 and 1914).

Mahinda Deegalle (born 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Ceylon, Harvard, and Chicago under Wendy Doniger and Frank E. Reynolds, he has held posts at IIBS, McGill, Harvard, Colgate, and Bath Spa University (~2002–2018).
Mahiro Ito (born 1968) is a Buddhist studies scholar who succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021. Ito has held professorships at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Maho Iuchi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Otani University by 2008 and served as a visiting researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (attested 2010).
Mai Mishiro is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held an attested post at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science in 2011 and at Waseda University in 2016.

Makio Takemura (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Mie University, University of Tsukuba, and Toyo University, where he served as president (2009–2020), as well as positions at several other institutions.

Makio Ueno works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning a PhD from Otani University by 2009, Ueno held posts there as an assistant professor (attested 2010–2012) and faculty member (attested 2022), alongside affiliation with the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Makoto Kitada is an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed doctoral studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. Kitada held a post at Toho Kenkyukai (attested 2008–2010) and is a base member at Osaka University (attested 2026).

Makoto Nagai (1881–1970) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1934–1942), Nihon, Toyo, and Kamakura Women's universities, and president of Chuo Shoka Junior College (1951).
